doc.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998

title: A career of luck: rehearsal pianist, MGM, radio and television
summary: Henderson sums up his career: rehearsal pianist, wartime flying, MGM, radio, then stumbling into television at NBC.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Well it’s a business of luck you know. I started as a rehearsal pianist in films and World War II came and I flew the great war as we say, and I came back and went to MGM. The grass was growing and the cottage, the bungalow as we called them where I used to rehearse these great stars, the hinges were broken. It looked like the great Midwest during the dust bowl. And I thought whatever happened you know.
You kind of got in on the ground floor again?
So then I drifted into radio. And then I saw radio disappear. I’ve been through all these train wrecks.
And you’ve come out on the other side.

And then somehow, well I was working at NBC with Sinatra actually. We were doing Lucky Strike and a Vice President of NBC walked up one day and said, “What are you going to do?” It’s a great straight line, isn’t it? And I said, “Well I’ll probably go back to Hollywood and try to make a living.” I didn’t know what I was going to do. Then he said, “Why don’t you stay here” — I love this line — he said “we’re going to do television.” I love that line. And I stayed there and stumbled into television.
